sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The window is a step change, not a smooth compound: revenue grew 125.9% in FY2024, 114.2% in FY2025 and 65.5% in FY2026 [D338][D393][D448].
The FY2024 step came from Data Center revenue up 217% on Hopper GPU shipments for LLM training and inference [P22][P23].
FY2025 growth was driven by data center compute and networking for accelerated computing and AI, with Hopper demand for the full year [P16].
FY2026 growth was driven by data center compute and networking platforms, with Blackwell architectures the majority of Data Center revenue [P10].
Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue and contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% growth [D620][D622][D448].
Within it, Data Center computing grew 59% on Blackwell demand and Data Center networking grew 142% on the NVLink ramp for GB200 and GB300 systems [P8].
Networking contributed 14.1pp of FY2026 growth against 46.1pp from Compute [D636][D629].
Operating income grew 60.1% against revenue growth of 65.5%, an incremental operating margin of 57.3% [D449][D448][D475].
Operating costs grew 24.8pp slower than revenue in FY2026, at 40.7% [D476][D468].
Operating margin was 60.4% in FY2026, above the 32.8% window median but below the 62.4% FY2025 high [F50][D813][D812].
The FY2026 margin fell 2.0pp, with cost of revenue taking 3.9pp off and R&D and SG&A adding back 1.3pp and 0.6pp [D463][D477][D478][D479].
The R&D increase was driven by a 29% rise in compensation and benefits and a 79% rise in compute and infrastructure [P5].
Net margin of 55.6% sat 4.8pp below the 60.4% operating margin, as other income of $11.1 billion partly offset a 15.1% tax rate [F70][F50][X120][D434].
Other income rose on unrealized gains in non-marketable and publicly-held equity securities, including the Intel investment [P3].
Operating cash flow of $102.7 billion was 0.86x net income in FY2026, below the 1.00x of FY2017 [F100][F60][D435][D8].
Free cash flow of $96.7 billion was a 44.8% margin, against a 44.4% window median [F110][D432][D822].
Capex of $6.04 billion was 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A, up from 0.71x in FY2024 [F105][D431][D437][D327].
Inventory grew 112.3% and receivables 66.8%, both faster than the 65.5% revenue growth [D474][D473][D448].
Net cash fell to $2.14 billion, 1.0% of revenue, from $34.7 billion a year earlier [D441][D442][D386].
Investing cash use rose on higher purchases of equity investment securities and a non-exclusive license agreement with Groq [P1].
Net cash of 1.0% of revenue still ranked at the 83rd percentile of six semis peers, whose median was -13.9% [D442][D844][D845].
Buybacks and dividends of $41.1 billion were 42.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 1.2% [D443][D444][D470].
China revenue fell 21.4% in FY2026, a 4.1pp drag on growth, after contributing 20.9pp in FY2025 [D545][D546][D543].
A 9.1% China share against 19.2% a year earlier is a concentration risk the filings do not explain [D544][D541].
Two direct customers represented 22% and 14% of FY2026 revenue, both mainly in Compute & Networking [P6].
Customer concentration of that size makes the revenue base sensitive to single-buyer ordering shifts.
The Graphics segment was 44.1% of revenue and fell 25.0% in FY2023 [D753][D754].
That episode shows how fast a large product line can reverse, though Graphics was only 10.4% of FY2026 revenue [D746].
Whether operating margin holds above the 60.4% FY2026 level or slips toward the 32.8% window median, in the FY2027 10-K [F50][D813].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue recovers from 1.0% or falls further, in the FY2027 10-K [D442].
Whether China revenue reverses its 21.4% FY2026 decline from the $19.7 billion base, in the FY2027 10-K [D545][S24].
